capitals.name: Dumat al-Jandal
capitals.note: The page has the Qedarites 'centred in their capital Dumat al-Jandal' in Al-Jawf; the dot is the gazetteer's Dawmat al Jandal. The page does not date the capital before the second half of the 9th century.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Qedar; the Neo-Assyrian shape of -700 and the Neo-Babylonian and Achaemenid shapes cover the Jawf only at their edges, if at all. The page gives no area; it places the Qedarites in the Wadi Sirhan and the Jauf depression with Dumat as their main centre (second half of the 9th century) and bordering western Babylonia in the 7th. Al Jawf Province is the core reading.

wars.name: Battle of Qarqar (Qedar's camelry)
wars.outcome: Gindibu of Qedar led 1,000 camelry in the coalition of Aram-Damascus and Israel against Shalmaneser III at Qarqar in 853 BC.
wars.note: The page gives no land result.

wars.name: Samsi's revolt and Tiglath-Pileser III's campaign

zones.text: Qedar 'centred in their capital Dumat al-Jandal' with the Wadi Sirhan and the Jauf depression (page); Al Jawf Province (105,000 km2, 35.0-41.8 E, 28.2-31.7 N) is the researcher's reading

wars.outcome: Samsi pledged allegiance after the 734 campaign and rebelled in 733; the Assyrian king attacked Qedar at Mount Saqurri and forced her to flee to Wadi Sirhan; she later paid 125 white camels.
wars.note: The camel tribute is undated on the page.

wars.name: Sennacherib's campaign against Qedar

zones.text: Qedar 'centred in their capital Dumat al-Jandal' with the Wadi Sirhan and the Jauf depression (page); Al Jawf Province (105,000 km2, 35.0-41.8 E, 28.2-31.7 N) is the researcher's reading

wars.outcome: Sennacherib campaigned against Qedar and captured Dumat in 691 BC, during the reigns of Te'elhunu and Haza'il; Hazael then paid tribute until Sennacherib's death and visited Nineveh in 681.
wars.note: The page gives no return of Dumat; Qedar's status after 691 is a bridge.

wars.name: Yauta's revolts against Esarhaddon

zones.text: Qedar 'centred in their capital Dumat al-Jandal' with the Wadi Sirhan and the Jauf depression (page); Al Jawf Province (105,000 km2, 35.0-41.8 E, 28.2-31.7 N) is the researcher's reading

wars.outcome: Yauta rebelled during Esarhaddon's Egypt campaign in 671 BC and was defeated; he returned in 669, rebelled again and was later imprisoned by Ashurbanipal (undated).
wars.note: Wahb's revolt against Yauta was suppressed in 676-673 BC.

wars.name: Nabonidus against the Qedarites and Dadan
wars.outcome: Nabonidus defeated the Qedarites, who had backed Dadan, before Cyrus; the Neo-Babylonian dossier has him take Tayma c. 553.
wars.note: The page gives no land change.

certainty.note: The page names the Wadi Sirhan, the Jauf and later the Negev, Sinai and northern Hejaz but no frontier; the shapes are provincial readings.

sources.title: Qedar
sources.note: Infobox 9th century to 1st century BC; Dumat al-Jandal; Gindibu at Qarqar 853; Zabibe 738; Samsi 733 and 716; Sennacherib 691; Esarhaddon 671; Ashurbanipal 645; Nabonidus 553; Achaemenid Empire 539; Geshem 445; Artaxerxes III 343 'possibly'; no area.

notes: Cliopatria has no Qedar; the Neo-Assyrian -700, Neo-Babylonian and Achaemenid imperial shapes may overlap the Jawf and the Negev, so the renderer should treat Qedar as a tinted tributary tile where it falls inside them. The page gives no founding date (infobox '9th century BC'); 853 is the first dated king. The vassal sequence is a summary of dated tribute and revolts: the page does not give a settlement after 645 or any Neo-Babylonian suzerainty (Nabonidus 553 only). Persian-period status (vassal under the satrapy of Arabaya) is the page's account; the end at 343 rests on 'possibly' and conflicts with the infobox's 1st century BC end and with Qedarites at Gaza in 332. Neo-Assyrian dossier (me-02) has no Qedar tribute events, only the Mu'na Arabs after 734, so the 738/716 vassal events here have no counterpart there. Nabataeans (Cliopatria row -164..105) is the successor by the page's infobox. AlUla/Dedan (Dadan), Tayma and Hegra are not in the gazetteer. Page budget: one page.
